evals.prompt: I updated an existing Skill in the jay-skills repository. Synchronize it, publish it to main, and reinstall it; you have my approval for the complete workflow.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the repository Skill as authoritative, validates and documents only the affected Skill, creates an honest Chinese Conventional Commit, pushes it, installs only that Skill globally without an agent flag, and verifies the canonical installation.
expectations: The repository target is used as the source of truth.
Unrelated worktree changes are preserved and excluded from the commit.
The authorized publish branch is the remote default branch used by installation.
The install command uses --skill, --global, and --yes without --agent.
Success requires matching content under ~/.agents/skills/<skill-name>.
Existing complete release authorization is reused without a redundant confirmation.

evals.prompt: The installed copy of an existing Skill has local edits that differ from its jay-skills source. Sync it and publish the update.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not overwrite the repository from the installed copy. It presents the meaningful diff and ports only confirmed intended changes into the repository source before validation and publication.
expectations: The installed copy is treated as an artifact rather than authority.
The existing repository target is never recursively replaced.
A material conflict is surfaced for confirmation before publication.

evals.prompt: I changed a Skill but have not authorized a Git push or a global installation. Run sync-skill-to-jay.
evals.expected_output: The agent prepares the authorized local inspection and validation with a reviewable diff, then asks once for the missing publication and installation authority without performing external writes.
expectations: The requested confirmation names the Skill, repository, publish branch, push, and installation.
No commit, push, remote change, or global install occurs before approval.

evals.prompt: The Skills CLI exited successfully and reported that PromptScript does not support global installation. The selected Skill was copied to ~/.agents/skills and exactly matches the pushed repository version. Complete the workflow.
evals.expected_output: The agent accepts the canonical installation as successful, reports the unrelated PromptScript adapter issue as a warning, and does not require Codex- or Claude-specific symlinks.
expectations: Canonical file-set and content verification determines success.
The PromptScript message is reported as a non-blocking warning.
No ~/.codex/skills or ~/.claude/skills link is required or created.

evals.prompt: I authorized publishing an updated Skill, but the jay-skills checkout is currently on a feature branch while the repository default branch and installer source are main.
evals.expected_output: The agent stops before committing and asks for explicit direction to switch or merge because pushing the feature branch would not update the default branch consumed by installation.
expectations: The current branch and upstream are checked against the remote default branch.
The agent does not publish and install mismatched branches under the original approval.
The agent does not silently switch, merge, or force-push.

evals.prompt: I approved the complete main-branch publish and install workflow. The configured HTTPS push failed only because credentials are unavailable, and the existing GitHub SSH identity is verified as the expected account.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the already authorized one-time SSH URL fallback without changing origin, fetches the configured remote to refresh origin/main, and continues only after the remote-tracking branch matches the new commit.
expectations: The bounded SSH fallback does not trigger a redundant confirmation.
Identity mismatch, new credential setup, or a remote change still requires a new decision.
The configured origin URL is not rewritten.
